summary: Canary model aliasing caused free-tier offset to be applied to async batch jobs, producing invoice discrepancy
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that two large async batch jobs (run by org AtlasSearch Inc.) processed on 2026-03-08 had free-tier offset lines appear on the finalized invoice for March, but the matching credits are attributed to a decommissioned canary API key alias.

Impact:
- Invoice shows -$4,200 credit line but AtlasSearch says credits are missing from their active subaccount ledger; net invoice amount appears correct but internal accounting for the customer is inconsistent.
- Customer-facing operations team cannot reconcile credits to job IDs; potential renewed distrust and escalation to finance.

Environment:
- Production (us-east-1)
- Customer org uses dedicated capacity (enterprise) with mixed routing: hosted fallback enabled.

Steps to reproduce / observed pattern:
1) AtlasSearch submitted two async batch jobs (job IDs withheld per customer) on 2026-03-08 at ~03:12 and ~03:43 UTC targeting atlas-search-v1 alias.
2) During a canary rollout, atlas-search-v1 was temporarily aliased to atlas-search-v1-canary for a subset of traffic.
3) Router assigned billing_tag based on the alias name at request-handshake time.
4) Postback/reconciler consumed usage events and applied free-tier offsets using the billing_tag present in the event stream.
5) When the canary alias was decommissioned, billing_tag entries remained associated with the old alias (decommissioned API key), so offsets landed on the inactive tag.

Observed behavior:
- Final invoice shows the expected reduction in total due, but AtlasSearch's internal ledger (active subaccount) lacks the matching credit entries.
- Support trace shows the credits exist in ledger index but are linked to the decommissioned alias tag (api-key: as-canary-2026-02).

Expected behavior:
- Free-tier offsets and credits should always be attributed to the active billing entity for the job (org + subaccount), not to transient alias strings created during rollouts.

Relevant logs and artifacts:
- Router logs (router-us-east-2026-03-08-03.log) show handshake lines with billing_tag=as-canary-2026-02 for 03:12:14.
- Postback events shard (postback-prod-us-east/2026-03-08/part-12) contains offset record id offset-ff23a.
- Billing reconciler job #2026-03-10-02 run produced reallocation token reallo-7381 failing a sanity check (error E_BILL_TAG_MISMATCH).
- Slack thread: #support (link: slack.com/archives/CH_SUPPORT/12345)
- Customer provided a screenshot of finalized invoice line items (attached to ticket in UI).
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Support (Ava): Logged initial report from AtlasSearch. Requested job IDs, sample request headers, and permission to run ledger queries. Customer granted access for a 48h window.
2026-03-10 11:03 - SRE (Ravi): Pulled router traces and confirmed alias billing_tag present in handshake for both job windows. Opened INT-8892 to trace reconciler ingestion timing.

2026-03-10 14:20 - Customer (Malcolm from AtlasSearch): Provided job IDs JOB-20260308-11 and JOB-20260308-12 and CSV of async submission times. Asks for a timeline and whether invoice will be corrected automatically or needs manual crediting.
2026-03-11 08:07 - Billing (Priya): Ran ledger query and found ~4200 USD in credits under tag 'as-canary-2026-02'. Preparing manual backfill plan if engineering patch is required.

2026-03-12 10:56 - Engineering (Ravi): Deployed hotfix to router to include stable 'billing_entity_id' in handshake metadata and published PR github.com/redwood/router/pull/572. Running backfill job to move affected offsets to correct entity.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: out-of-order postback ingestion caused offsets to be applied to stale tag.
Status: Partially true — ingestion ordering exacerbated the issue but root cause is attribute selection logic for billing attribution.

Key finding: router used alias string for billing attribution when aliasing was active. That alias string is transient and can be decommissioned; reconciler indexes credits by the raw tag string and does not reconcile to org-level billing_entity_id.

Query run: SELECT count(*) FROM offsets WHERE billing_tag='as-canary-2026-02' AND created_at::date='2026-03-08' returned 2 rows totaling 4200.
Query run: SELECT ledger_entity FROM jobs WHERE job_id IN ('JOB-20260308-11','JOB-20260308-12') returned ledger_entity 'org-AtlasSearch/sub-01'.
Discrepancy: offsets linked to alias tag instead of ledger_entity.
Reconciler log snippet: 'E_BILL_TAG_MISMATCH: offset offset-ff23a attributed to tag as-canary-2026-02 not found on current ledger for org-AtlasSearch at reconciliation time'.
Repro test in staging: created alias->model switch and confirmed offsets applied to alias-tag in staging reconciler. Created a regression test failing prior to patch.
resolution_notes: Workaround (applied 2026-03-11): Billing team executed a manual reallocation using internal tool (acct-tool backfill --tag as-canary-2026-02 --target org-AtlasSearch/sub-01 --ids offset-ff23a,offset-ff24b). Credits now appear on customer's active subaccount ledger. Customer notified and provisional invoice adjustment issued.

Code fix (deployed 2026-03-12): Router handshake now attaches stable 'billing_entity_id' (org+subaccount) to every request in addition to human-readable alias. PR: github.com/redwood/router/pull/572. Reconciler updated to prioritize billing_entity_id for attribution (reconciler PR: github.com/redwood/reconciler/pull/1283).

Backfill: Reconciler backfill job ran 2026-03-12 03:30 UTC and re-allocated 5 affected offset records totaling $4,200. Backfill audit log: backfill-2026-03-12-03. Customer ledger reconciled and finance issued a credit memo and email to customer contact (Malcolm).

Follow-ups: Add integration test to ensure reconciler prefers billing_entity_id over alias string; add metric and alert on 'offsets-attributed-to_decommissioned_tags' threshold; include a short postmortem in Confluence page linked above.

Customer communication: Sent detailed timeline and confirmation of credit allocation 2026-03-12 12:10 UTC. Customer acknowledged and requested confirmation when automated fixes have monitoring in place.
Status: Monitoring. Billing and SRE to watch for similar events during upcoming canary rollouts this quarter.
